Please, don't take me as some narcissistic prick, I'm a graphic designer starting to fall love with this site, and since i don't have any bitcoin (for now) I thought that I could give back some love to the site in form of constructive criticism. So here I go:

I really love the overall design ideas for the site: minimalistic approach, subtle contrasts to discern key parts of the page, buttons and links that stand out but don't get in the way, etc. But after seeing quite some times our mascot in the dreaded "downtime" page, and taking some closer look to the anagram, I stumbled upon some minor quirks that can have a real impact on the visual quality of the site.

 

First of all, colors.And I think this is the most important of all: I don't know how many of you have some sort of color-blindness condition, but I just tossed the anagram into a color-blindness simulator, and the colors for upvoat and downvoat turned to the same purple hue. Even if the main attractive is the shape of the symbol, this is a big problem, since with the current color scheme you can't actually relate to the action it represents just by the color. I'll explain myself: I don't like to put "The other site" into discussion, but they had their colors well established and thought out. Take for example any upvote or downvote gif, in quite a lot of them you are differentiating its meaning just by the color, and with the voat's current color scheme it can be quite a challenge if the upvoat/downvoat is not clearly up or down. I suggest rethinking one of the colors, for contrast sake.

 

Next thing is the anagram, wich I personally love a big lot. But analyzing it closely you can see there is a little problem with the tracking between letters, specially between A-T. Personally I'll open a bit the space between the V-O-A, so the A-T fits right in. Another thing that bothers me is the thick gray outline, because it does not quite relate to the overall design of the site. Every other line around here is a barely perceivable hairline, so if you look at the anagram it just "stands out" too much, it even has a blurry feel to it. It has to be a more elegant way to make it visible against the background.

 

And last is our mascot. I love love love the idea of a goat as a mascot for the site, it's crazy, cute, energic, etc. Anything we can relate to without hesitate. But for me, the solution needs a bit more work. It seems that who made the design just came up with this drawing and didn't try more elaborated ideas. Personally, I'd only use the goat's face and work from that upwards; If the body is really necessary, I'll look more into proportions, symmetries and so.

 

Sorry for the big post, and thanks for reading! Shall we discuss design now?

 

tl;dr: Colors need contrast. Goat needs overhaul.

How does mining Bitcoin work?

Bitcoin is based on a so-called blockchain that basically follows a set of rules, regarding the content of the blocks. So to extend the chain, you have to find a block that "fits", which is (by design) very difficult. Finding this block is called mining, and finding the next block promises a reward of (iirc) currently 25 Ƀ. The practical reason behind this is that the entire transaction history withing the Bitcoin network is "engraved" into the blockchain, so by inspecting it you can see all past trades and also which "account" has how much money at a given point, like the present. There are a lot more details to it, but that are the basics.

Is Bitcoint mining profitable anymore?

If you have to ask, probably not really. I like to compare it to growing weed to sell it. You might be able to grow some and sell it for a couple of bucks, but it takes a lot of investment, both in terms of time and money, to make a real business out of it, and it also comes at a risk. Bitcoin mining is done using specialized "mini-CPUs", so-called ASICs, nowadays. If you read something about GPU-mining, or even CPU-mining, it is old and not correct anymore, both of these are not viable by a great margin anymore. ASICs are small devices that usually plug into a USB-port and have hardware that is designed especially to mine bitcoin at great speed while consuming as little power as possible. For mining to be profitable, you need up-to-date hardware, which costs money, and you need to mine more Bitcoin than you are paying for the power you need to do so. There are a lot of calculators on the web that can tell you at which point you will have made the money back you invested for a device like this, but as faster and more effecient ones come out yearly, it is all a gamble.

TL;DR Getting into mining nowadays is not really the best idea, it is a wide field consisting of people who invested a lot into it and know everything about it. You are not going to get in there and make "free money".

If you actually want to make money off of Bitcoin, and are somewhat knowledgable with computers (which I assume as you have a RasPi), get into the Bitcoin community and look around how everything works, than start a service that complements that, like a Bitcoin donation service for YouTubers or Twitch streamers (just an example). Bitcoin is still very young and there are a lot of vacancies in the industry surrounding it.
